destinations.description: Vigan is the best-preserved example of a planned Spanish colonial town in Asia, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its centerpiece is Calle Crisologo, a cobblestone street lined with ancestral houses that now hold shops, cafes, and museums. The city blends Filipino, Chinese, and Spanish influences in its architecture, crafts, and food.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a 7 to 9 hour bus from Manila to Vigan via Partas, Viron, or Dominion; flights to Laoag plus a 1.5 hour van ride are a faster option.
destinations.name: Vigan

places.description: The famous half-kilometer cobblestone street lined with ancestral houses from the Spanish era. Best explored on foot or by calesa, especially in the early morning or at night when the street lamps glow.
places.name: Calle Crisologo

places.description: A mini zoo and animal sanctuary owned by the Singson family, with tigers, ostriches, and reptiles. Admission is free and the grounds include a butterfly garden and picnic areas.
places.name: Baluarte Mini Zoo

places.description: A historic hilltop bell tower in nearby Bantay that served as a watchtower during colonial times. Climb to the top for panoramic views of Vigan and the surrounding plains.
places.name: Bantay Church Bell Tower

places.description: The ancestral home of former president Elpidio Quirino, preserved as a museum with antique furniture and memorabilia. It gives a vivid look at ilustrado life in old Vigan.
places.name: Syquia Mansion

places.description: Ride a horse-drawn calesa past the heritage houses, the cathedral, and the plazas with a kutsero who doubles as a guide. A signature Vigan experience, especially after sunset.
places.name: Calesa Ride Around Heritage Village

places.description: A nightly fountain show at Plaza Salcedo with water, lights, and music telling the story of Ilocos. Shows usually run in the evening and draw big local crowds on weekends.
places.name: Dancing Fountain Show

places.description: A beloved Vigan institution serving Ilocano classics like pinakbet, bagnet, and Vigan longganisa in a cozy ancestral house setting. A reliable first stop for heritage-town dining.
places.name: Cafe Leona

places.description: A row of stalls near Plaza Burgos frying the famous Vigan empanada with orange rice-flour crust, longganisa, egg, and papaya. Pair it with sukang Iloko for the full experience.
places.name: Vigan Empanadaan

places.description: The first museum-hotel in the Philippines, blending Ilocano heritage interiors with a fine art collection. Located steps from Calle Crisologo, it is the premium stay in the heritage core.
places.name: Hotel Luna

places.description: A mid-range inn near the heritage village with clean, comfortable rooms and helpful staff. A practical base for travelers who spend most of the day exploring on foot.
places.name: Cordillera Inn

places.description: The best place to buy Vigan longganisa, bagnet, basi vinegar, and woven abel products at local prices. Go early in the morning for the freshest selection of native delicacies.
places.name: Vigan Public Market

places.description: Tricycles cover short hops between the heritage village, Baluarte, and the Bantay bell tower. Agree on the fare before boarding, especially for trips outside the town center.
places.name: Tricycle

destinations.tagline: A living Spanish colonial city with cobblestone streets

transport.notes: Negotiate the route and duration with the kutsero before the ride starts
transport.useCase: Sightseeing around the heritage village and plazas

transport.notes: The most common way to reach sights outside walking distance
transport.useCase: Short trips to Baluarte, Bantay, and nearby sights

transport.notes: Partas, Viron, and Dominion run regular trips, including overnight buses
transport.useCase: Manila to Vigan and onward to Laoag or Pagudpud

transport.notes: The heritage village is compact and best experienced on foot
transport.useCase: Exploring Calle Crisologo and the heritage core

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come for the romantic old-world streetscape, heritage houses you can walk through, and iconic Ilocos food like empanada and longganisa.

destinations.bestTime: November to February for cool weather; March to May for clearer skies
destinations.description: Sagada is a cool highland town in the Cordilleras known for its hanging coffins, limestone caves, and sea-of-clouds viewpoints. It has a laid-back backpacker culture with cafes, weaving shops, and pine-forested trails. The town blends indigenous Igorot traditions with a relaxed mountain-town vibe.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a bus to Bontoc from Manila or Baguio, then a jeepney or van to Sagada; direct Coda Lines buses also run from Manila.
destinations.name: Sagada

places.description: A cliffside burial site where coffins of Sagada elders hang from limestone walls, reached by a short trail from the town center. A local guide is required and shares the stories behind this centuries-old tradition.
places.name: Echo Valley and Hanging Coffins

places.description: Sagada's most famous cave, with towering limestone formations, underground pools, and chambers reached by rappelling and wading. The standard 2-hour spelunking route needs a guide and basic fitness.
places.name: Sumaguing Cave

places.description: A sunrise viewpoint famous for its sea of clouds rolling over the valley below. Arrive before dawn and dress warmly, since temperatures drop sharply at this elevation.
places.name: Kiltepan Peak Sunrise Viewpoint

places.description: A tall, powerful waterfall reached by a scenic trek through rice terraces from Banga-an village. Swimming is allowed in the catch basin on calm days.
places.name: Bomod-ok Falls

places.description: A pre-dawn trek to rolling hills with panoramic sunrise views over the Cordillera mountains. Local guides lead the hike and can arrange the connecting Blue Soil Hills side trip.
places.name: Marlboro Hills Sunrise Trek

places.description: A local weaving house selling handwoven bags, blankets, and garments made on traditional looms. You can watch the weavers at work before buying directly from the shop.
places.name: Sagada Weaving

places.description: A cozy spot famous for its homemade yoghurt served with granola, honey, and local fruits. It also serves hearty mountain meals that hit the spot after a day of trekking.
places.name: Sagada Yoghurt House

places.description: A Sagada institution baking its signature lemon pie along with other pastries and bread. A classic stop for dessert or pasalubong to bring home.
places.name: Sagada Lemon Pie House

places.description: A rustic inn with a cafe serving good coffee and comfort food, popular with backpackers. The pine-surrounded setting keeps it cool and quiet at night.
places.name: Rock Inn and Cafe

places.description: One of Sagada's long-running inns with simple rooms and a restaurant, close to the town center. A dependable mid-range choice for first-time visitors.
places.name: Shamrock Tavern Inn

places.description: A small private museum of Igorot artifacts, weapons, and ritual objects collected over decades. It is a quick but meaningful stop to understand local culture before the treks.
places.name: Ganduyan Museum

places.description: Jeepneys connect Sagada town to Bontoc and nearby villages like Banga-an and Aguid. Schedules are limited, so confirm departure times at the tourism office.
places.name: Jeepney

destinations.tagline: Misty mountain town of hanging coffins and caves

transport.notes: Limited daily schedules; check the tourism office for departure times
transport.useCase: Travel between Sagada, Bontoc, and trailhead villages

transport.notes: Vans can also be chartered for Kiltepan and Marlboro Hills sunrise trips
transport.useCase: Bontoc to Sagada transfers and group tours

transport.notes: Most of Poblacion is walkable, but bring a jacket for chilly mornings
transport.useCase: Town center, Echo Valley, and nearby cafes

transport.notes: Coda Lines runs direct Manila to Sagada trips on select schedules
transport.useCase: Manila or Baguio to Sagada via Bontoc

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come for the Echo Valley hanging coffins, Sumaguing Cave spelunking, and sunrise views over the clouds at Kiltepan and Marlboro Hills.

destinations.bestTime: March to May for green terraces; November to February for cool weather
destinations.description: Banaue is the gateway to the Ifugao rice terraces, often called the Eighth Wonder of the World, carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago. The town sits in a valley ringed by terraced amphitheaters, with nearby villages like Batad and Bangaan holding the most spectacular clusters. It is the classic starting point for Cordillera terrace trekking.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take an overnight bus from Manila to Banaue via Ohayami Trans; from Banaue, jeepneys and tricycles reach nearby villages.
destinations.name: Banaue

places.description: The classic postcard viewpoint overlooking vast terraced slopes from the main road. Souvenir stalls and photo spots with traditional Ifugao costumes line the viewing area.
places.name: Banaue Rice Terraces Viewpoint

places.description: A UNESCO-listed cluster of terraces shaped like a giant amphitheater, reached by a jeepney ride and a downhill trek from the saddle. It is widely considered the most beautiful terrace formation in the Cordilleras.
places.name: Batad Amphitheater Rice Terraces

places.description: A towering waterfall at the base of the Batad terraces, reached by a steep trek down from the village. The cold, powerful cascade is a rewarding finish after the terrace hike.
places.name: Tappiya Falls

places.description: A traditional Ifugao village nestled in a bowl of rice terraces, also part of the UNESCO listing. A short trek from the road brings you into the village for homestays and cultural immersion.
places.name: Bangaan Village

places.description: A museum of Ifugao artifacts including bulul rice gods, weapons, and traditional clothing. It is a compact stop that deepens the terrace experience with cultural context.
places.name: Banaue Museum

places.description: A longer trek through the Hungduan cluster of terraces, known for stone-walled paddies and hot springs along the route. Less crowded than Batad, with equally dramatic scenery.
places.name: Hapao Rice Terraces Trek

places.description: A lodge restaurant serving Filipino and continental dishes with terrace views from its dining area. A convenient dinner spot for travelers staying in the town center.
places.name: People's Lodge Restaurant

places.description: A native-style restaurant near the viewpoint road serving local Ifugao dishes and grilled meats. The nipa-hut dining setup adds to the highland atmosphere.
places.name: Native Village Inn Restaurant

places.description: The landmark hotel in town with native-inspired architecture and sweeping views over the valley. It offers the most comfortable rooms and amenities in Banaue proper.
places.name: Banaue Hotel

places.description: Simple family-run homestays inside Batad village, some in traditional native huts overlooking the amphitheater. Basic but atmospheric, with home-cooked meals available.
places.name: Batad Village Homestays

places.description: Woodcarving shops along the main road selling bulul statues, woven textiles, and miniature terrace models. Haggle politely and compare a few stalls for the best carvings.
places.name: Banaue Souvenir Shops

places.description: Tricycles handle short trips around town and to nearby trailheads like the viewpoint and Tam-an. For Batad and Hapao, jeepneys are the standard ride.
places.name: Tricycle

destinations.tagline: Home of the ancient rice terraces carved by hand

transport.notes: Often chartered per group; arrange through your hotel or the tourism office
transport.useCase: Banaue to Batad saddle, Bangaan, and Hapao trailheads

transport.notes: Hire for the day when visiting the viewpoint, Tam-an, and Ducligan hot spring
transport.useCase: Short trips around Banaue town and nearby viewpoints

transport.notes: Ohayami Trans runs overnight buses from Sampaloc, Manila
transport.useCase: Manila to Banaue overnight

transport.notes: The town center is compact; many restaurants and shops are walkable
transport.useCase: Getting around Banaue Poblacion

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come to see the sweeping Banaue viewpoint terraces and trek to Batad's amphitheater-like terraces and Tappiya Falls.

destinations.bestTime: October to March for surfing; November to February for cooler weather
destinations.description: Baler is the birthplace of Philippine surfing and the surf capital of Luzon's east coast, facing the Pacific Ocean. Its star is Sabang Beach, where the 1979 film Apocalypse Now was shot, but it also packs waterfalls, rock formations, a giant balete tree, and the historic Siege of Baler church into one small town. It is an easy weekend escape from Manila with a laid-back surf-town feel.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a 5 to 6 hour bus from Manila to Cabanatuan, then a 3 to 4 hour van to Baler; direct JoyBus and Genesis buses also run from Manila.
destinations.name: Baler

places.description: Baler's main surf beach with gentle rolling waves ideal for beginners and longboarders. Surf schools and board rentals line the shore, and the beach comes alive at sunrise with learners catching their first waves.
places.name: Sabang Beach

places.description: A waterfall a short drive from town, reached by an easy walk through riverside scenery. A refreshing dip here is a classic add-on to the Diguisit rock formations trip.
places.name: Diguisit Falls

places.description: Known as the Mother Falls, this 140-foot cascade is reached by a scenic 30 to 45 minute trek from Barangay Ditumabo. It is one of Aurora's most photographed natural attractions.
places.name: Ditumabo Mother Falls

places.description: A centuries-old balete tree with massive roots you can climb on, located in the neighboring town of Maria Aurora. The 20 to 30 minute drive from Baler is a staple of the town's countryside tour.
places.name: Millennium Balete Tree

places.description: A 17th-century church famous as the site of the Siege of Baler, where Spanish soldiers held out for nearly a year after the Philippine revolution. The adjacent museum tells the story of the last Spanish garrison in the country.
places.name: Baler Church and Museo de Baler

places.description: A secluded cove with white sand and clear water, reached by a boat ride from Sabang or a trek over the hills. It is quieter than Sabang and popular for day-trip picnics.
places.name: Dicasalarin Cove

places.description: A garden restaurant serving Filipino comfort food with Baler touches, known for its relaxed open-air setting. A favorite dinner spot after a day of surfing.
places.name: Kusina Luntian

places.description: A beachfront grill serving seafood, sizzling dishes, and cold drinks steps from the surf. Live music nights make it a go-to hangout for the surf crowd.
places.name: Baler Surfer Grill

places.description: The landmark beachfront resort on Sabang Beach with a pool, surf shop, and direct access to the waves. The top choice for a comfortable surf holiday in Baler.
places.name: Costa Pacifica

places.description: A popular mid-range inn near the beach with clean rooms and a friendly surf-town atmosphere. Walking distance to surf schools and restaurants along the strip.
places.name: Bay's Inn

places.description: A local shop selling woven abaca products, suman, and Aurora souvenirs. A good stop for pasalubong before heading back to Manila.
places.name: Baler Souvenir Shops

places.description: Tricycles are the main way to reach the falls, the balete tree, and the rock formations, often hired for half-day tours. Agree on the itinerary and price with the driver beforehand.
places.name: Tricycle Tour

destinations.tagline: The birthplace of Philippine surfing on the Pacific coast

transport.notes: The standard way to tour the falls, balete tree, and rock formations
transport.useCase: Town tours and nearby attractions

transport.notes: Genesis Transport and JoyBus run direct services from Cubao and Pasay
transport.useCase: Manila to Baler direct or via Cabanatuan

transport.notes: Public vans connect Cabanatuan to Baler for the last leg
transport.useCase: Cabanatuan to Baler transfers

transport.notes: Some attractions like Dicasalarin Cove are reached by boat from Sabang
transport.useCase: Dicasalarin Cove and coastal day trips

transport.notes: Sabang strip and the town center are easily walkable
transport.useCase: Sabang Beach and Poblacion exploration

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come to learn surfing on Sabang Beach's beginner-friendly waves and to tour the Mother Falls, Diguisit rock formations, and the historic Baler Church.

destinations.bestTime: November to April for calm seas; avoid the June to September monsoon
destinations.description: Hundred Islands is a protected national park in Alaminos, Pangasinan, made up of 123 islands and islets scattered across Lingayen Gulf. Only a few are developed for visitors, with Governor's Island's view deck, snorkeling spots, and caves as the highlights. Island hopping here is one of the classic Luzon weekend trips, easy to pair with Bolinao.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a 5 to 6 hour bus from Manila to Alaminos, Pangasinan, then a tricycle to Lucap Wharf where tour boats depart.
destinations.name: Hundred Islands

places.description: The island with the famous 123-step view deck overlooking the scattered islets of the national park. It also hosts a zipline and a narrow channel connecting it to Virgin Island at low tide.
places.name: Governor's Island

places.description: A small island with a shallow lagoon popular for swimming and beginner snorkeling. Its calm waters make it a favorite family stop on the island-hopping route.
places.name: Children's Island

places.description: An island known for Imelda Cave and a natural swimming pool enclosed by rock formations. It is one of the most scenic stops for photos and cliff jumping.
places.name: Marcos Island

places.description: A developed island with cottages, camping grounds, and snorkeling areas. Many tour packages use it as the lunch and swimming stop of the day.
places.name: Quezon Island

places.description: A cave on Marcos Island where sunlight pours through an opening onto the water below, popular for cliff jumping and swimming. The drop into the water is a rite of passage for Hundred Islands visitors.
places.name: Imelda Cave

places.description: A 546-meter zipline flying from Governor's Island across the water, with views of the islets below. It is one of the most thrilling add-ons to the island-hopping tour.
places.name: Hundred Islands Zipline

places.description: A seafood restaurant near Lucap Wharf serving fresh catches, grilled squid, and Filipino classics. A natural lunch stop before or after the island-hopping tour.
places.name: Maxine by the Sea

places.description: A local eatery in Alaminos town known for Pangasinan dishes like pigar-pigar and bangus preparations. A good taste of the province beyond the wharf restaurants.
places.name: Alaminos Town Eateries

places.description: A well-known hotel in Alaminos with a pool and restaurant, a short ride from Lucap Wharf. The most comfortable base for visitors doing the Hundred Islands tour.
places.name: Island Tropic Hotel

places.description: Budget inns near the wharf area catering to island-hopping tourists with simple, clean rooms. Ideal for early departures since the wharf is minutes away.
places.name: Lucap Wharf Area Inns

places.description: Souvenir stalls near Lucap Wharf selling shell crafts, dried seafood, and Pangasinan delicacies like tupig. Stock up on pasalubong right after your boat returns.
places.name: Lucap Souvenir Stalls

places.description: Licensed motorized boats leave Lucap Wharf for guided island-hopping circuits of 3 to 5 islands. Register at the tourism office and choose between small, medium, or large boats based on group size.
places.name: Island Hopping Boat

destinations.tagline: 123 scattered islets made for island hopping

transport.notes: Register at the Hundred Islands tourism office; rates depend on boat size
transport.useCase: Island hopping around the national park

transport.notes: The jump-off point for all island tours
transport.useCase: Alaminos town to Lucap Wharf

transport.notes: Five Star and Victory Liner run Manila to Alaminos routes
transport.useCase: Manila to Alaminos, Pangasinan

transport.notes: Boats can also stop at snorkeling and kayaking stations on request
transport.useCase: Snorkeling, kayaking, and helmet diving

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come for affordable island hopping across dozens of islets, the Governor's Island view deck, and snorkeling in the clear waters of Lingayen Gulf.

destinations.bestTime: February to May for clear Mayon views; June to October is the rainy season
destinations.description: Legazpi is the gateway city to Mayon Volcano, the world's most perfect cone, which dominates every skyline view in town. Beyond the volcano, Legazpi offers ATV adventures on Mayon's slopes, the haunting Cagsawa Ruins, and some of Bicol's best food. It is a compact city that works as both a destination and a base for Albay tours.
destinations.howToGetThere: Fly 1 hour from Manila to Legazpi via Bicol International Airport; buses take 10 to 12 hours.
destinations.name: Legazpi

places.description: The bell tower ruins of a church buried by Mayon's 1814 eruption, now the most iconic photo spot in Bicol. The park around it has ATV jump-off points and Mayon-facing viewpoints.
places.name: Cagsawa Ruins

places.description: Ride an ATV across lava fields and riverbeds on Mayon's slopes, passing through landscapes shaped by past eruptions. Tour lengths range from short 45-minute runs to full-day black lava wall treks.
places.name: Mayon ATV Adventure

places.description: A 156-meter hill in the city with a zipline and the best close-up sunrise views of Mayon Volcano. On clear mornings the volcano fills the entire horizon from the viewing deck.
places.name: Lignon Hill Nature Park

places.description: A baroque church perched on a hill in Daraga with Mayon Volcano perfectly framed behind it. One of the oldest stone churches in the Bicol region, built in the 1700s.
places.name: Daraga Church

places.description: A serene lake in Camalig with bamboo rafts and floating cottages, famous for its mirror-like reflections of Mayon. A quieter, greener alternative to the Cagsawa crowds.
places.name: Sumlang Lake

places.description: A 5-kilometer seaside boulevard with jogging paths, food stalls, and Mayon views across the water. The go-to sunset promenade for locals and visitors alike.
places.name: Legazpi Boulevard

places.description: The home of the famous sili ice cream, flavored with Bicol's fiery chili, plus pili desserts and Bicol dishes. A must-visit for adventurous eaters in Albay.
places.name: 1st Colonial Grill

places.description: A local favorite serving Bicolano classics like Bicol express, laing, and pinangat with generous spice levels. Hearty servings at prices locals are happy to pay.
places.name: Waway's Restaurant

places.description: The premier hotel in Legazpi, perched on a hill with sweeping views of Mayon Volcano and Albay Gulf. An infinity pool and full amenities make it the splurge stay in the city.
places.name: The Oriental Legazpi

places.description: A modern mid-range hotel near the city center with clean rooms and a rooftop pool. Convenient for business and leisure travelers exploring Albay.
places.name: Hotel St. Ellis

places.description: The city's pasalubong center for pili nuts, pili candies, and Bicol handicrafts. One stop covers most of the souvenir list for Albay.
places.name: Legazpi Pasalubong Center

places.description: Jeepneys and tricycles cover routes between Legazpi, Daraga, and Camalig, including the Cagsawa and Sumlang Lake stops. For Mayon tours, most operators include transfers in the package.
places.name: Tricycle and Jeepney

destinations.tagline: The city under the perfect cone of Mayon Volcano

transport.notes: Direct 1-hour flights from Manila to Bicol International Airport
transport.useCase: Manila to Legazpi flights

transport.notes: Book through accredited operators in Cagsawa or Ligñon Hill
transport.useCase: Mayon lava trail adventures

transport.notes: Fares vary by distance; jeepneys are cheaper for fixed routes
transport.useCase: Getting around Legazpi, Daraga, and Camalig

transport.notes: Shared vans run the Legazpi to Donsol and Legazpi to Naga routes
transport.useCase: Day trips to Donsol and other Albay towns

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come for postcard views of Mayon Volcano, the Cagsawa Ruins, ATV rides on lava trails, and Bicol's famously spicy food.

destinations.bestTime: March to June for calm seas; avoid the July to October typhoon season
destinations.description: Caramoan is a remote peninsula in Camarines Sur famous as a filming location for multiple seasons of Survivor. Its limestone islands, hidden lagoons, and white-sand beaches are reached only by island-hopping boats from Paniman Beach. Raw and undeveloped, it rewards travelers who do not mind the long journey.
destinations.howToGetThere: Fly or bus to Naga, take a van to Sabang port, a boat to Guijalo, then a jeepney to Caramoan town; island tours depart from Paniman Beach.
destinations.name: Caramoan

places.description: A small island with white sand, clear water, and limestone cliffs, famous from Survivor seasons. One of the standard stops on the Caramoan island-hopping circuit.
places.name: Lahos Island

places.description: An island with a hidden lagoon enclosed by limestone karsts, reached by swimming through a narrow opening at low tide. One of Caramoan's most photographed natural formations.
places.name: Matukad Island

places.description: A tiny island with a sandbar, a small chapel, and a giant cross on its limestone peak. The short climb rewards visitors with sweeping views of the surrounding islands.
places.name: Minalahos Island

places.description: The jump-off beach for Caramoan island hopping, with boats lined up along its shore. The surrounding area also has coves and snorkeling spots worth exploring.
places.name: Gota Beach

places.description: The 17th-century parish church of Caramoan, dedicated to St. Michael the Archangel. Its red-brick facade is one of the oldest church structures in Camarines Sur.
places.name: St. Michael the Archangel Church

places.description: A full-day boat circuit visiting Lahos, Matukad, Minalahos, and other islets with stops for swimming and snorkeling. Boats are arranged at Paniman Beach through the tourism office.
places.name: Caramoan Island Hopping Tour

places.description: The resort restaurant at Gota Beach serving Filipino dishes and fresh seafood with sea views. The most reliable full-service dining option near the island jump-off point.
places.name: Gota Village Resort Restaurant

places.description: Simple carinderias in the town proper serving Bicol dishes like laing and Bicol express at local prices. Stock up on meals here before heading to Paniman Beach.
places.name: Caramoan Town Eateries

places.description: The go-to resort for Caramoan visitors, set on a hillside overlooking the islands. It offers the most comfortable rooms near the island-hopping jump-off point.
places.name: Gota Village Resort

places.description: A secluded cove resort with a private beach, cottages, and kayaking, reachable by boat. A quieter alternative for travelers who want to stay right on the water.
places.name: Tugawe Cove Resort

places.description: The town market sells pili nuts, dried fish, and Bicol handicrafts at local prices. A practical stop for pasalubong before the long trip back.
places.name: Caramoan Public Market

places.description: Motorized boats are the only way to reach the islands, arranged through the tourism office at Paniman. On land, tricycles and habal-habal connect the town, Paniman, and Guijalo port.
places.name: Island Hopping Boat

destinations.tagline: The Survivor-famous peninsula of hidden island lagoons

transport.notes: Book through the Caramoan tourism office; rates depend on boat size
transport.useCase: Island hopping to Lahos, Matukad, and Minalahos

transport.notes: Sabang to Guijalo boats connect to vans bound for Naga
transport.useCase: Naga to Caramoan multi-leg transfer

transport.notes: The standard ride within town and to Paniman Beach
transport.useCase: Caramoan town to Paniman and Guijalo

transport.notes: Motorbikes for hire for rougher roads around the peninsula
transport.useCase: Reaching remote beaches and viewpoints

destinations.whyPopular: Travelers come for Survivor-famous island hopping to limestone islets and hidden lagoons, plus some of the most untouched beaches in Luzon.

destinations.bestTime: November to April for dry weather; Underground River tours run year-round
destinations.description: Puerto Princesa is Palawan's capital and the gateway to the world-famous Underground River, one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature. Beyond the subterranean river, the city offers Honda Bay island hopping, firefly watching on the Iwahig River, and a relaxed city center with good seafood. It is the natural first stop on any Palawan itinerary.
destinations.howToGetThere: Fly 1.5 hours from Manila or Cebu to Puerto Princesa International Airport; ferries also connect from Manila and Coron.
destinations.name: Puerto Princesa

places.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring an 8.2-kilometer navigable underground river through a limestone cave. Paddle boats glide past cathedral-like chambers filled with stalactites and bats.
places.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River

places.description: A group of islets including Cowrie, Starfish, and Luli Islands, known for white sand and excellent snorkeling. The standard island-hopping circuit is the city's most popular day tour after the Underground River.
places.name: Honda Bay Island Hopping

places.description: A nighttime paddle-boat tour where thousands of fireflies light up mangrove trees along the river. The star-filled sky over the water makes it one of Palawan's most magical evening experiences.
places.name: Iwahig Firefly Watching

places.description: A park with butterfly gardens, colorful blooms, and a good view deck over the city. Its in-house bakeshop is famous for hopia and other pastries worth taking home.
places.name: Baker's Hill

places.description: A WWII memorial marking the site where American prisoners of war were killed in 1944. The small plaza and museum are a solemn reminder of Palawan's wartime history.
places.name: Plaza Cuartel

places.description: The city's main Catholic church with its distinctive blue facade, built in the late 1800s. It anchors the old town area near Plaza Cuartel and the baywalk.
places.name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral

places.description: A beloved seafood restaurant where diners eat barefoot on sand floors under nipa roofing. Famous for fresh grilled seafood and its charming, rustic atmosphere.
places.name: Ka Lui Restaurant

places.description: A seafront restaurant on stilts over the water, perfect for sunset dinners of Filipino and seafood dishes. Live acoustic music adds to the bayfront atmosphere.
places.name: Badjao Seafront Restaurant

places.description: A modern resort-style hotel with pools and gardens, popular with families and tour groups. Well located for city tours and airport transfers.
places.name: Princesa Garden Island Resort

places.description: A beachfront resort in Sabang near the Underground River wharf, with a pool facing the sea. Ideal for travelers who want to be close to the national park instead of the city.
places.name: Daluyon Beach and Mountain Resort

places.description: A weaving center where you can watch artisans make colorful placemats and bags from indigenous fibers. Buying here directly supports the local weaving community.
places.name: Binuatan Creations Weaving Center

places.description: Tricycles are everywhere and handle most city trips, with multicabs serving fixed routes. For Sabang and the Underground River, book a van tour that includes permits and transfers.
places.name: Tricycle

destinations.tagline: Gateway to the world-famous Underground River

transport.notes: Daily 1.5-hour flights from Manila, Cebu, and Clark
transport.useCase: Getting to Puerto Princesa

destinations.bestTime: October to March for surfing; November to February for the best waves
destinations.description: San Juan, La Union is the surf capital of the North, where the laid-back beach town of Urbiztondo draws surfers, digital nomads, and weekenders from Manila. Beyond the waves, it has a thriving cafe and food scene, from famous coffee shops to beachfront party spots. It is the easiest surf trip from Manila at just 4 to 5 hours by bus.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a 4 to 5 hour bus from Manila to San Juan via Partas, Viron, or Victory Liner.
destinations.name: San Juan, La Union

places.description: The main surf beach of La Union with consistent beach-break waves suitable for beginners and intermediates. Surf schools line the shore, and the sunset sessions here are legendary.
places.name: Urbiztondo Beach

places.description: A famous surf-town cafe credited with kickstarting La Union's coffee culture, serving slow-bar coffee and brunch. Expect lines on weekends, but the people-watching is worth it.
places.name: El Union Coffee

places.description: A beachfront food park with container stalls, live DJs, and fire dancers, and one of the birthplaces of Elyu's party scene. The place to be after the sun goes down on weekends.
places.name: Flotsam and Jetsam

places.description: A multi-tiered waterfall in nearby San Gabriel, reached by a trek through rice fields and forest trails. The deep natural pools are perfect for cliff jumping and swimming.
places.name: Tangadan Falls

places.description: Take a lesson from one of the many accredited surf schools along Urbiztondo Beach. Instructors provide boards and an hour of coaching, with most beginners standing up by the end.
places.name: Surf Lessons at Urbiztondo

places.description: A go-to spot for Mexican-Filipino fusion, famous for its tacos and nachos served steps from the sand. A staple of the Urbiztondo food crawl.
places.name: Tagpuan

places.description: A boutique beachfront resort with stylish rooms, a pool, and a restaurant facing the surf. One of the most photographed stays in Elyu for its design and beach access.
places.name: Kahuna Beach Resort and Spa

places.description: A mid-range beach resort with a pool and direct access to Urbiztondo Beach. A comfortable base within walking distance of the surf schools and cafes.
places.name: Costa Villa Beach Resort

places.description: Surf shops along the beach road sell boards, wax, rash guards, and Elyu-branded apparel. A good place to gear up before lessons or grab souvenirs after.
places.name: Urbiztondo Surf Shops

places.description: The town market sells fresh produce, dried fish, and La Union delicacies like tupig and basi. A glimpse of local life beyond the surf strip.
places.name: San Juan Public Market

places.description: A cliffside viewpoint and small park overlooking the surf break, popular for sunrise and sunset photos. A short walk from the main beach strip.
places.name: Urbiztondo Point View Deck

places.description: Tricycles connect the beach strip, the town proper, and nearby attractions like Tangadan Falls. Most of Urbiztondo itself is walkable on foot.
places.name: Tricycle

destinations.tagline: The surf capital of the North with a buzzing beach scene

destinations.bestTime: November to June for whale sharks; November to May for calm seas
destinations.description: Donsol is the whale shark capital of the Philippines, where gentle butanding gather in its plankton-rich waters from November to June. Swimming alongside these giants under strict interaction rules is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Beyond the whale sharks, Donsol offers firefly river tours, manta ray diving, and quiet beaches.
destinations.howToGetThere: Fly to Legazpi, then take a 1 to 1.5 hour van or bus to Donsol; buses from Manila take 10 to 12 hours.
destinations.name: Donsol

places.description: The main whale shark interaction site, where spotters locate butanding and boats bring swimmers to snorkel beside them. Strict rules keep the experience safe for both visitors and the gentle giants.
places.name: Donsol Whale Shark Interaction

places.description: Snorkel or free-dive beside whale sharks under the guidance of trained Butanding Interaction Officers. November to June offers the best chances of sightings.
places.name: Swimming with Whale Sharks

places.description: A peaceful night cruise on the Ogod River where fireflies cluster in the riverside trees. The calm water and dark skies make it a romantic end to a whale shark day.
places.name: Ogod River Firefly Watching

places.description: A world-class dive site off nearby Ticao Island known for manta ray encounters and cleaning stations. Advanced divers visit from Donsol for day trips during the season.
places.name: Manta Bowl Dive Site

places.description: The registration and briefing center for all whale shark interactions, with exhibits about butanding conservation. Every tour starts here with an orientation from the tourism office.
places.name: Donsol Tourism Center

places.description: A beachfront resort restaurant serving Bicol dishes and fresh seafood with views of Donsol Bay. A convenient meal stop after the morning whale shark tour.
places.name: Vitton Beach Resort Restaurant

places.description: A beach resort restaurant known for Filipino comfort food and grilled seafood in a garden setting. A relaxing dinner spot for divers and whale shark watchers.
places.name: Amor Farm Beach Resort Restaurant

places.description: A popular beachfront resort in Donsol with a pool, dive shop, and whale shark tour arrangements. The most established stay for butanding season visitors.
places.name: Vitton Beach Resort

places.description: A beach resort with native-style cottages, a garden, and easy access to the whale shark jump-off points. A quieter, mid-range alternative on the coast.
places.name: Amor Farm Beach Resort

places.description: The town market sells dried fish, pili products, and Bicol delicacies at local prices. A good stop for pasalubong and snacks before the trip back to Legazpi.
places.name: Donsol Public Market

places.description: Tricycles connect the town center, resorts, and the tourism center, and can be hired for half-day tours. Vans handle the Legazpi to Donsol transfer.
places.name: Tricycle
